tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

input.content:
<#
Backup-Content.ps1 - Copia diaria del proyecto del juego (el Content/ no tiene historial en git).
Espeja con robocopy /MIR el proyecto SIN Binaries, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache ni Build.
Pensado para la tarea programada "JamContentBackup" (SETUP F1c punto 5).

Uso:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools\Jam\Backup-Content.ps1 `
      -ProjectDir C:\GameJam\MiJuego -Dest C:\Users\<user>\OneDrive\JamBackup

Salida: <Dest>\<NombreProyecto>\ (espejo) y <Dest>\backup.log (una linea por ejecucion + log de robocopy).
OJO: /MIR borra en el destino lo que ya no existe en el origen. Por eso el script se niega a
correr si el destino esta dentro del proyecto (o al reves), o si el destino es la raiz de un disco.
Exit: 0 bien, 1 parametros invalidos, 2 robocopy fallo (codigo >= 8).
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$ProjectDir,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Dest
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ProjectDir -PathType Container)) { Write-Host "No existe el proyecto: $ProjectDir"; exit 1 }
$src = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $ProjectDir).Path.TrimEnd('\')
$uproj = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $src -Filter *.uproject -File)
if ($uproj.Count -ne 1) { Write-Host "Se esperaba exactamente un .uproject en $src (hay $($uproj.Count))"; exit 1 }
$name = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($uproj[0].Name)

$destRoot = [IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Dest).TrimEnd('\')
if ($destRoot -match '^[A-Za-z]:$') { Write-Host "El destino no puede ser la raiz de un disco: $Dest"; exit 1 }
$srcCmp = $src.ToLowerInvariant() + '\'
$dstCmp = $destRoot.ToLowerInvariant() + '\'
if ($dstCmp.StartsWith($srcCmp) -or $srcCmp.StartsWith($dstCmp)) { Write-Host "Origen y destino se solapan: $src / $destRoot"; exit 1 }

$target = Join-Path $destRoot $name
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($target)
$log = Join-Path $destRoot 'backup.log'
$start = Get-Date
Add-Content -LiteralPath $log -Value ("==== {0} {1} -> {2}" -f $start.ToString('s'), $src, $target)

& robocopy $src $target /MIR /XD Binaries Intermediate Saved DerivedDataCache Build .vs .git /R:2 /W:5 /NP /NFL /NDL "/LOG+:$log" | Out-Null
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$secs = [int]((Get-Date) - $start).TotalSeconds
Add-Content -LiteralPath $log -Value ("==== fin robocopy={0} ({1} s)" -f $code, $secs)
if ($code -ge 8) { Write-Host "FALLO robocopy (codigo $code). Ver $log"; exit 2 }
Write-Host "Copia OK (robocopy $code, $secs s) -> $target"
exit 0

content.thinking: The Incoming folder inherits full control for Authenticated Users from C:\, which would let network users delete files. I'm writing an idempotent script to break that inheritance, for you to review and run elevated.

input.content:
<#
Setup-IncomingShare.ps1 - Configura la carpeta compartida de entrada de assets (SETUP F1c).
REQUIERE PowerShell ELEVADA. Idempotente: se puede correr varias veces.

Antes (lo hace la persona, el agente no escribe contrasenas):
  net user jamshare * /add          (pide la contrasena; luego darsela a las otras maquinas)

Que hace:
  1. Perfil de la red Wi-Fi indicada -> Privado.
  2. Firewall: dos reglas propias (grupo "JamIncoming"), solo perfil Privado y solo LocalSubnet:
     SMB TCP 445 y ping ICMPv4. NO toca las reglas de "Compartir archivos e impresoras" de
     Windows (vienen como "Private, Public" en un solo objeto; activarlas abriria tambien Publico).
  3. NTFS en <JamRoot>\Incoming: corta la herencia de C:\ (que da Modificar = BORRAR a
     "Authenticated Users") y deja:
       SYSTEM, Administradores, <usuario actual>: control total
       <ShareUser>: en la raiz solo leer/recorrer (sin herencia);
                    en ASSETS\ y LAPTOP\: crear archivos y carpetas, escribir, anexar, leer, atributos.
                    SIN Eliminar ni Eliminar subcarpetas y archivos.  _Imported\: sin acceso.
       OWNER RIGHTS: solo lectura (si no, el dueno de un archivo nuevo podria cambiar su ACL
                    y darse permiso de borrar).
  4. Recurso compartido "Incoming": Cambiar para <ShareUser>, Total para el usuario actual.
  5. Tarea programada "JamContentBackup" (diaria 04:00, DESACTIVADA) que llama a Backup-Content.ps1.
     Activarla cuando exista el proyecto: ajustar -ProjectDir en la accion y Enable-ScheduledTask.

Limitacion conocida: sin permiso de borrar tampoco se puede RENOMBRAR. Herramientas que escriben
un temporal y luego lo renombran sobre el final fallaran al sobrescribir. robocopy y la copia del
Explorador sobrescriben en el sitio (sirve). -Uninstall no existe: ver "Deshacer" al final.

Uso:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\GameJam\Tools\Jam\Setup-IncomingShare.ps1 `
      -WifiProfile Romelt_5G -BackupDest "$env:USERPROFILE\OneDrive\JamBackup"
#>
param(
    [string]$JamRoot = 'C:\GameJam',
    [string]$ShareUser = 'jamshare',
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$WifiProfile,
    [string]$BackupDest = (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'OneDrive\JamBackup'),
    [string]$ProjectDirPlaceholder = 'C:\GameJam\CAMBIAR_POR_EL_PROYECTO',
    [string]$OwnerUser = $env:USERNAME
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$isAdmin = ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal][Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
if (-not $isAdmin) { Write-Host 'Hace falta una PowerShell ELEVADA.'; exit 1 }
if (-not (Get-LocalUser -Name $ShareUser -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Write-Host "No existe el usuario local '$ShareUser'. Crealo primero: net user $ShareUser * /add"; exit 1
}
$inc = Join-Path $JamRoot 'Incoming'
foreach ($s in 'ASSETS', 'LAPTOP', '_Imported') { [void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Join-Path $inc $s)) }
$pc = $env:COMPUTERNAME
$su = "$pc\$ShareUser"
$ou = "$pc\$OwnerUser"

Write-Host '== 1. Perfil de red'
Set-NetConnectionProfile -Name $WifiProfile -NetworkCategory Private
Get-NetConnectionProfile -Name $WifiProfile | ForEach-Object { "  $($_.Name): $($_.NetworkCategory)" }

Write-Host '== 2. Firewall (grupo JamIncoming, solo Private + LocalSubnet)'
Get-NetFirewallRule -Group 'JamIncoming' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Remove-NetFirewallRule
[void](New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Jam Incoming - SMB-In (TCP 445)' -Group 'JamIncoming' -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 445 -Profile Private -RemoteAddress LocalSubnet -Action Allow)
[void](New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Jam Incoming - Ping (ICMPv4 echo)' -Group 'JamIncoming' -Direction Inbound -Protocol ICMPv4 -IcmpType 8 -Profile Private -RemoteAddress LocalSubnet -Action Allow)
Get-NetFirewallRule -Group 'JamIncoming' | ForEach-Object { "  $($_.DisplayName) | $($_.Profile) | Enabled=$($_.Enabled)" }

Write-Host '== 3. NTFS'
# SIDs para no depender del idioma de Windows: S-1-5-18 SYSTEM, S-1-5-32-544 Administradores, S-1-3-4 OWNER RIGHTS.
& icacls $inc /inheritance:r /grant:r '*S-1-5-18:(OI)(CI)(F)' '*S-1-5-32-544:(OI)(CI)(F)' "${ou}:(OI)(CI)(F)" "${su}:(RX)" '*S-1-3-4:(OI)(CI)(RX)' | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "icacls raiz fallo ($LASTEXITCODE)" }
foreach ($s in 'ASSETS', 'LAPTOP') {
    $p = Join-Path $inc $s
    & icacls $p /reset /T /C | Out-Null    # que hereden solo de la raiz recien fijada
    & icacls $p /grant:r "${su}:(OI)(CI)(RD,WD,AD,REA,WEA,X,RA,WA,RC,S)" | Out-Null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "icacls $s fallo ($LASTEXITCODE)" }
}
& icacls (Join-Path $inc '_Imported') /reset /T /C | Out-Null
& icacls $inc
foreach ($s in 'ASSETS', 'LAPTOP', '_Imported') { & icacls (Join-Path $inc $s) }

Write-Host '== 4. Recurso compartido'
if (Get-SmbShare -Name 'Incoming' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Remove-SmbShare -Name 'Incoming' -Force }
[void](New-SmbShare -Name 'Incoming' -Path $inc -ChangeAccess $su -FullAccess $ou -Description 'Jam: entrada de assets (escribir si, borrar no)')
Get-SmbShareAccess -Name 'Incoming' | ForEach-Object { "  $($_.AccountName): $($_.AccessRight) $($_.AccessControlType)" }
Write-Host "  Ruta para las otras maquinas: \\$pc\Incoming\  (o por IP si el nombre no resuelve)"

Write-Host '== 5. Tarea programada JamContentBackup (desactivada)'
$script = Join-Path $JamRoot 'Tools\Jam\Backup-Content.ps1'
$arg = "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File `"$script`" -ProjectDir `"$ProjectDirPlaceholder`" -Dest `"$BackupDest`""
$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument $arg
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 4am
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries -AllowStartIfOnBatteries
$principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId $ou -LogonType Interactive -RunLevel Limited
[void](Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'JamContentBackup' -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings -Principal $principal -Force)
[void](Disable-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'JamContentBackup')
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'JamContentBackup' | ForEach-Object { "  $($_.TaskName): $($_.State)" }
Write-Host 'LISTO.'
<#
Deshacer (despues de la jam, PowerShell elevada):
  Remove-SmbShare -Name Incoming -Force
  Get-NetFirewallRule -Group JamIncoming | Remove-NetFirewallRule
  Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName JamContentBackup -Confirm:$false
  icacls C:\GameJam\Incoming /reset /T
  net user jamshare /delete
#>

toolUseResult.originalFile:
<#
Package-Jam.ps1 - Empaqueta el juego para la entrega de la jam y arma el zip.
Receta probada en UE 5.9.0 (CL 60351404) el 2026-11-09:
  - UAT BuildCookRun Win64 Development con -build -cook -stage -pak -iostore -archive.
  - NO usar -nocompileeditor: con plugins no-default activos (p. ej. AllToolsets) el cook
    busca <Proyecto>Editor.target y falla si no se compilo.
  - Config/DefaultGame.ini con bUseZenStore=False (en la maquina de assets el cook murio
    escribiendo en la carpeta de Zen; causa no confirmada). El script lo comprueba.
  - El zip EXCLUYE los .pdb (simbolos de depuracion, ~340 MB que no hacen falta).
  - Limite de la jam: zip < 1 GB, nombre TeamName_GameName.zip.

Uso:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Package-Jam.ps1 -Project D:\Jam\MiJuego\MiJuego.uproject -ZipName Equipo_Juego
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Project,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$ZipName,
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [string]$Config = 'Development'
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$buildDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Build'
$logFile = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\uat_package.log'
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Split-Path $logFile -Parent))

$game = Join-Path $projDir 'Config\DefaultGame.ini'
$zenOff = (Test-Path $game) -and (Select-String $game -Pattern '^\s*bUseZenStore\s*=\s*False' -Quiet)
if (-not $zenOff) {
    Write-Host 'AVISO: falta bUseZenStore=False en Config/DefaultGame.ini. Se agrega.'
    Add-Content $game "`r`n[/Script/UnrealEd.ProjectPackagingSettings]`r`nbUseZenStore=False`r`n"
}

$uat = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Build\BatchFiles\RunUAT.bat'
$uatArgs = @('BuildCookRun', "-project=`"$Project`"", '-platform=Win64', "-clientconfig=$Config",
          '-build', '-cook', '-stage', '-pak', '-iostore', '-archive', "-archivedirectory=`"$buildDir`"",
          '-noP4', '-utf8output', '-unattended')
Write-Host "UAT -> $logFile"
& cmd.exe /d /c "`"$uat`" $($uatArgs -join ' ') > `"$logFile`" 2>&1"
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
Get-Content $logFile -Tail 4
if ($code -ne 0) {
    Write-Host "FALLO UAT (exit $code). Primeras lineas de error:"
    Select-String $logFile -Pattern 'Error:|Exception|Cook failed' | Select-Object -First 15 | ForEach-Object Line
    exit $code
}

$win = Join-Path $buildDir 'Windows'
$zip = Join-Path $projDir "$ZipName.zip"
if (Test-Path $zip) { Remove-Item $zip -Force }
Remove-Item (Join-Path $win '*\Saved') -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
$z = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::Open($zip, 'Create')
try {
    Get-ChildItem $win -Recurse -File | Where-Object { $_.Extension -ne '.pdb' } | ForEach-Object {
        [void][System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::CreateEntryFromFile($z, $_.FullName, $_.FullName.Substring($win.Length + 1), 'Optimal')
    }
} finally { $z.Dispose() }
$mb = [math]::Round((Get-Item $zip).Length / 1MB, 1)
Write-Host "ZIP: $zip ($mb MB)"
if ($mb -ge 1024) { Write-Host 'FALLO: el zip supera 1 GB (limite de la jam). Usar butler o recortar contenido.'; exit 2 }
exit 0

content.text:
Everything I can do on my own has passed. What's left needs you: installing Claude Code and creating the `jamshare` user.

**Passed, with evidence:**
- **B1 System:** Windows 11 Home 26200, i9-13900HX (24 cores), 31.7 GB of RAM, RTX 4080 Laptop with 12 GB of VRAM, NVMe drive. `JAM_MACHINE=CENTRAL` is set.
  - **Note:** only **134 GB free on C:**, below the doc's 150 GB minimum.
- **B2 Compiler:** the only MSVC installed was **14.51**, which the engine bans. I installed the 14.50 LTSC component, and UBT now reports `Using Visual Studio 14.50.35737 toolchain ... Windows 10.0.26100.0 SDK`. That version is in the allowed range, and UBT skipped 14.51 on its own.
- **B3 Tools:** git 2.55, git-lfs 3.7.1, gh 2.103.3, FFmpeg 9.0.2, OBS 33.0 and 7-Zip are installed.
  - butler v15.32.0 isn't in winget. I downloaded it from itch.io's official site (the file is signed by itch corp) and put it in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\butler`, on your user PATH. I didn't put it in `Tools\` so its binaries don't end up in the repo.
- **B4 Unreal:** 5.9.0, Changelist 60351404, the same build as the assets machine. The plugins and templates are present.
- **T1 Editor MCP:** the server came up in 65 s and the protocol test passed 5/5, with 4 tools, ~128 toolsets and `/Temp/Untitled_1`. The Editor closed cleanly in 6 s.
- **T2 C++ build:** `Result: Succeeded` in 57 s.
- **T3 Packaging:** the Blueprint project built (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`) into a **385.8 MB** zip in 2 min 18 s. The packaged game booted to `LoadMap(/Game/ThirdPerson/Lvl_ThirdPerson)` with 0 fatal errors. The C++ project also packaged, at **311.5 MB**.
- **T4.2 Dev log hooks:** installed at user level, 6 events.

**A bug I fixed in the kit:** `Package-Jam.ps1` failed on any project without a `Config\` folder. I added one line to [Package-Jam.ps1](Tools/Jam/Package-Jam.ps1) and synced it to `JamKit`. **The assets machine's kit doesn't have this fix yet.**

**New files for F1c:**
- [Backup-Content.ps1](Tools/Jam/Backup-Content.ps1): tested. It refuses a destination that overlaps the project or is a drive root.
- [Setup-IncomingShare.ps1](Tools/Jam/Setup-IncomingShare.ps1): not run yet. Two things in it you should know:
  - `Incoming` currently inherits a permission from `C:\` that would let the network user **delete** files, so the script cuts that inheritance.

# Pre-jam work declaration

The jam rules (Official Rules 7(h)) allow preparing AI tools, agent configurations, MCP settings, prompt libraries and scripts before **Nov 12, 2026 at 00:00 ET**, but not building the game. Anything made earlier must be declared. This file declares it. The full log of the preparation, with dates and results, is in `PREJAM_PREP.md`.

**No game content was created before the jam:** no levels, no mechanics, no game assets and no gameplay code.

## Tools and scripts prepared before the jam (2026-11-09 to 2026-11-11)
| Item | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code dev log hook | Logs every Claude Code event as JSONL | `.claude/hooks/devlog-hook.ps1`, `Devlog/.jamroot` |
| `Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` | Installs the hook in the Claude Code user settings | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1` | Wrapper that logs every run of an external agent | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1` | Extracts agent actions (MCP, Assistant, Canvas) from the Editor log | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `New-DevlogDay.ps1` | Builds the redacted daily draft | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Start-EditorMcp.ps1`, `Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, `Test-UnrealMcp.ps1` | Open, close and test the UE 5.9 Editor with MCP | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `Package-Jam.ps1` | Win64 packaging and submission zip (tested recipe) | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `AssetSearch` | Local semantic search over 37,668 licensed assets (public index `codepawl/asset-index`, EmbeddingGemma 2 embeddings). Contains no assets, only metadata | `Tools/AssetSearch/` |
| Dev log templates | `README.md`, `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, this file, `PREJAM_PREP.md` | `Devlog/` |
| Project `CLAUDE.md` | Working rules for the agents | root |

## Technical tests before the jam (no game content)
- 2026-11-09: the UE 5.9 Editor MCP server answered (handshake, toolset list and a real call) in an empty project.
- 2026-11-09: built an empty C++ module (only `IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE`) to validate the toolchain. The project was deleted.
- 2026-11-09: test packaging of Epic's ThirdPersonBP template (386 MB zip, boots correctly). The test project was deleted.
- 2026-11-10: MetaHuman Animator body capture from a single phone video, driven entirely over MCP, exported to the UE5 mannequin. The test video is a raw recording of a team member swinging a stick; it is not game content and will not be used in the game. Test project: `MHProbe59` (tooling probe only).
- (central machine setup: add the date and the result of `SETUP_REPORT.md` here)

## Prompts, prompt templates or assets prepared before the jam
- (none so far; anything prepared will be listed here with its date)

## AI tools we plan to use
- Claude Code (Anthropic): main agent for code and for the Editor through MCP.
- MetaHuman Animator (UE 5.9) + the Fab plugin "MetaHuman Animator Markerless Motion Capture" (Epic, free): body animation from single-camera video, tested on 2026-11-10 with a test take that is not game content.
- (to complete: Unreal Assistant, Unreal Canvas and its provider, Fab generation, Modly, ElevenLabs…)

# Pre-jam work declaration

The jam rules (Official Rules 7(h)) allow preparing AI tools, agent configurations, MCP settings, prompt libraries and scripts before **Nov 12, 2026 at 00:00 ET**, but not building the game. Anything made earlier must be declared. This file declares it. The full log of the preparation, with dates and results, is in `PREJAM_PREP.md`.

**No game content was created before the jam:** no levels, no mechanics, no game assets and no gameplay code.

## Tools and scripts prepared before the jam (2026-11-09 to 2026-11-11)
| Item | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code dev log hook | Logs every Claude Code event as JSONL | `.claude/hooks/devlog-hook.ps1`, `Devlog/.jamroot` |
| `Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` | Installs the hook in the Claude Code user settings | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1` | Wrapper that logs every run of an external agent | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1` | Extracts agent actions (MCP, Assistant, Canvas) from the Editor log | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `New-DevlogDay.ps1` | Builds the redacted daily draft | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Start-EditorMcp.ps1`, `Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, `Test-UnrealMcp.ps1` | Open, close and test the UE 5.9 Editor with MCP | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `Package-Jam.ps1` | Win64 packaging and submission zip (tested recipe) | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `Backup-Content.ps1` | Daily mirror copy of the game project without build folders (the `Content/` has no git history) | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `Setup-IncomingShare.ps1` | Sets up the LAN folder where the other machines drop assets (write allowed, delete denied) | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `AssetSearch` | Local semantic search over 37,668 licensed assets (public index `codepawl/asset-index`, EmbeddingGemma 2 embeddings). Contains no assets, only metadata | `Tools/AssetSearch/` |
| Dev log templates | `README.md`, `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, this file, `PREJAM_PREP.md` | `Devlog/` |
| Project `CLAUDE.md` | Working rules for the agents | root |

## Technical tests before the jam (no game content)
- 2026-11-09: the UE 5.9 Editor MCP server answered (handshake, toolset list and a real call) in an empty project.
- 2026-11-09: built an empty C++ module (only `IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE`) to validate the toolchain. The project was deleted.
- 2026-11-09: test packaging of Epic's ThirdPersonBP template (386 MB zip, boots correctly). The test project was deleted.
- 2026-11-10: MetaHuman Animator body capture from a single phone video, driven entirely over MCP, exported to the UE5 mannequin. The test video is a raw recording of a team member swinging a stick; it is not game content and will not be used in the game. Test project: `MHProbe59` (tooling probe only).
- 2026-11-11: central machine (CENTRAL) setup, details in `SETUP_REPORT.md`: 8 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 NEEDS-HUMAN (free disk space, and the cross-machine share test). Editor MCP 5/5, C++ build with MSVC 14.50.35737, test packaging of Epic's ThirdPersonBP template (385.8 MB zip, boots) and of an empty C++ module (311.5 MB), dev log hooks and wrapper verified. All test projects were deleted.

## Prompts, prompt templates or assets prepared before the jam
- (none so far; anything prepared will be listed here with its date)

- Claude Code (Anthropic): main agent for code and for the Editor through MCP.
- MetaHuman Animator (UE 5.9) + the Fab plugin "MetaHuman Animator Markerless Motion Capture" (Epic, free): body animation from single-camera video, tested on 2026-11-10 with a test take that is not game content.

Aquí tienes el prompt. Pégalo en el agente (Claude Code) de **PC Romelt** o de la **laptop**.

**Antes**, en esa máquina, **tú** abres la conexión con tu contraseña de `jamshare`, porque el agente no escribe contraseñas:

```bash
net use \\DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\Incoming /user:DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\jamshare *
```

Si dice que no encuentra la ruta de red, prueba con la IP: `\\192.168.31.188\Incoming`. Si tampoco funciona, desconecta NordVPN en esta PC.

````markdown
Tarea: prueba T5 de la carpeta compartida `Incoming` de la máquina CENTRAL (Epic AI MegaJam). Solo es una prueba de herramientas: no crees contenido del juego.

Contexto:
- La CENTRAL comparte `\\DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\Incoming\` (IP 192.168.31.188, misma red local). Usuario de red: `DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\jamshare`.
- Diseño de permisos: en `ASSETS\` y `LAPTOP\` se puede crear, escribir, sobrescribir y leer, pero NO borrar ni renombrar. En `_Imported\` no hay acceso. Solo la CENTRAL limpia.
- La persona ya abrió la sesión con `net use`. Tú NUNCA pides ni escribes contraseñas. Si no hay sesión, para y pídele que ejecute: `net use \\DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\Incoming /user:DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\jamshare *`.

Reglas:
- No cambies permisos, ni configuración de red, ni firewall, ni credenciales guardadas, ni en esta máquina ni en la CENTRAL.
- No borres nada fuera de la carpeta temporal que crees en %TEMP%. Los intentos de borrar en el recurso compartido SON la prueba: se espera que fallen.
- robocopy: los códigos de salida 0 a 7 significan éxito (1 = copió). Solo 8 o más es un error.
- Cada paso termina en PASS o FAIL con evidencia: la línea de salida o el mensaje de error literal.

Pasos (PowerShell):
0. `$m = $env:JAM_MACHINE`; si está vacío, léela con `[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('JAM_MACHINE','User')`. Tu subcarpeta es `ASSETS` si `$m` es ASSETS y `LAPTOP` si es LAPTOP. Si no es ninguna de las dos, para y pregunta. Define `$share = '\\DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\Incoming'` y `$dst = "$share\<subcarpeta>"`.
1. Red: `Test-NetConnection DESKTOP-RTEPFOL -Port 445`. Si falla, repítelo con 192.168.31.188 y, si eso funciona, usa la IP en `$share`. Muestra también `net use`.
2. Lectura: `Get-ChildItem $share`. Debe listar ASSETS, LAPTOP y _Imported.
3. Escritura: crea `%TEMP%\t5_jam\` con el archivo `t5_$m.txt` y el contenido "v1 el ñandú" (UTF-8). Ejecuta `robocopy <temp> $dst t5_$m.txt`. PASS si el código es menor que 8 y `Get-Content "$dst\t5_$m.txt" -Encoding UTF8` devuelve "v1 el ñandú".
4. Sobrescritura: cambia el archivo local a "v2 la cigüeña" y repite el robocopy. PASS si el archivo remoto dice "v2 la cigüeña".
5. Subcarpeta (Migrate de Unreal crea carpetas): `robocopy <temp> "$dst\t5_dir_$m" t5_$m.txt`. PASS si el archivo existe dentro.
6. Borrar (debe FALLAR): `Remove-Item "$dst\t5_$m.txt"` y, aparte, `cmd /c del "$dst\t5_$m.txt"`. PASS si los dos dan acceso denegado y el archivo sigue existiendo.
7. Borrar una carpeta (debe FALLAR): `Remove-Item "$dst\t5_dir_$m" -Recurse`. PASS si da acceso denegado y la carpeta sigue existiendo.
8. Renombrar (debe FALLAR, es esperado): `Rename-Item "$dst\t5_$m.txt" "t5_$m.renombrado.txt"`. PASS si da acceso denegado.
9. `_Imported` (debe FALLAR): intenta `Get-ChildItem "$share\_Imported"` y copiar ahí un archivo. PASS si los dos dan acceso denegado.
10. Limpieza local: borra solo `%TEMP%\t5_jam\`. NO intentes limpiar nada más en el recurso compartido.

Entrega:
- Una tabla con Paso | Estado | Evidencia y una línea final "T5 desde <$m>: PASS/FAIL".
- La lista exacta de rutas que dejaste en el recurso compartido, para que la CENTRAL las mueva a _Imported y las borre.
- Si algo falla, di la causa probable sin "arreglarla" tocando permisos.
````

Cuando el agente termine, pégame su tabla. Yo, desde aquí, compruebo que los archivos siguen en `Incoming`, los muevo a `_Imported` (el último paso de la prueba), los borro y marco T5 en el informe.

Es el mismo problema que tuviste con `net user`: `net` rechaza la línea antes de conectarse. Lo más probable es que al copiar desde el chat se cuele un carácter invisible, como un espacio especial. Olvídate de `net use`. Hay una forma más sencilla que no requiere escribir comandos.

**En la otra PC (PC Romelt o la laptop):**
1. Pulsa **Win + R**.
2. Escribe a mano `\\DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\Incoming` y pulsa Enter.
3. Windows te pedirá credenciales en su propia ventana:
   - Usuario: `DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\jamshare`
   - Contraseña: la que pusiste al crear `jamshare`
   - Marca **"Recordar mis credenciales"**.
4. Debe abrirse una ventana del Explorador con `ASSETS`, `LAPTOP` y `_Imported`. **No borres ni muevas nada ahí**: eso lo prueba el agente.

Con esa ventana abierta, la sesión de red ya existe y el agente puede usar la ruta directamente. Ya puedes pegarle el prompt.

**Si en el paso 2 sale "no se encuentra la ruta de red":**
- Prueba con la IP: `\\192.168.31.188\Incoming`.
- Si tampoco funciona, desconecta NordVPN en **esta** PC (la CENTRAL) y vuelve a intentarlo.
- Si sigue fallando, dime el mensaje exacto. Puedo comprobar desde aquí si llegan las conexiones.

Un detalle del prompt: en el paso 1 el agente mostrará `net use`. Con este método puede salir vacío o sin la letra de unidad, y es normal. Lo que cuenta es que el paso 2 (`Get-ChildItem` de la ruta) funcione.

## Pendientes para la persona (NEEDS-HUMAN)
- **Prueba T5 desde PC Romelt o la laptop** (misma red Wi-Fi o LAN que `Romelt_5G`, 192.168.31.0/24):
  1. `net use \\DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\Incoming /user:DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\jamshare *`. Si el nombre no resuelve, usar `\\192.168.31.188\Incoming`.
  2. `robocopy <carpeta> \\DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\Incoming\ASSETS t5.txt`: debe llegar.
  3. Repetirlo con el archivo modificado: debe sobrescribir.
  4. `del \\DESKTOP-RTEPFOL\Incoming\ASSETS\t5.txt`: debe dar **acceso denegado**.
  5. En la CENTRAL, mover `t5.txt` a `_Imported\` y borrarlo.
- **VPN NordVPN (NordLynx) activa:** puede ocultar esta PC a la red local. Si la prueba T5 no conecta, activa en NordVPN la opción de permitir la red local, o desconecta la VPN.
- **Copia diaria:** el 12 nov, cuando exista el proyecto, edita la acción de la tarea `JamContentBackup` (cambia `C:\GameJam\CAMBIAR_POR_EL_PROYECTO` por la carpeta del `.uproject`) y actívala con `Enable-ScheduledTask JamContentBackup`. El destino por defecto es `%USERPROFILE%\OneDrive\JamBackup`, en el mismo disco pero sincronizado a la nube.
- **`gh auth login`** (A7) y **`butler login`** (A8): no se han hecho.
- **Repo:** `git init` hecho en `C:\GameJam` sin ningún commit. El primer commit lo decides tú. `JamKit\` sigue en la raíz y **no está en `.gitignore`**: bórrala o ignórala antes del primer commit.
- **Claude Code:** la sesión se inició el 11 nov. Comprueba en qué fecha caduca (en ASSETS caducaba en plena jam).

## Observaciones (diferencias con la máquina de assets, tiempos de primera compilación de shaders, etc.)
- **MSVC:** una instalación de VS 2026 18.8 trajo solo 14.51 (prohibido), justo el riesgo que avisaba el documento. Con el componente LTSC, UBT eligió 14.50.35737 (en ASSETS fue 14.50.35735). La carpeta se llama `14.50.35717`, igual que en ASSETS.
- Hay también una instalación de **VS 2026 Insiders 18.9** sin herramientas de C++. UBT no la usa. No se tocó.
- **Tiempos:** primera apertura del Editor 65 s hasta MCP; primer empaquetado BP 2 min 18 s (ASSETS: 1 min 27 s, con los shaders ya compilados); empaquetado C++ 1 min 10 s.
- **Fallo del kit corregido:** `Package-Jam.ps1` fallaba si el proyecto no tenía `Config\` (`Add-Content` sobre una carpeta inexistente). Se añadió `CreateDirectory` antes. Corregido en `Tools\` y en `JamKit\`, **pero no en la copia de la máquina de assets.**
- **Borrador diario:** cuenta como "prompts del equipo" las notificaciones internas del arnés (`<task-notification>...`), lo que ensucia el borrador público. Conviene filtrarlas en `New-DevlogDay.ps1`.
- **Plugin de Claude Code con error:** un plugin instalado en el perfil de usuario lanza en cada `SessionEnd` el hook `session-lifecycle-hook.mjs`, que falla porque no hay `node`. No afecta a la bitácora, pero ensucia la salida. Instala Node o desactiva ese plugin.
- **Las sesiones de Claude Code Desktop también se registran:** esta misma sesión de setup quedó en `Devlog\raw`, porque los hooks son de usuario y la sesión estaba en `C:\GameJam`. Se borró en la limpieza según el documento. Lo que el hook escriba después de la limpieza (el cierre de esta sesión) puede volver a crear `Devlog\raw\CENTRAL\2026-11-11\`: bórralo antes del 12 nov.
- **Permisos de `Incoming`:** al no poder borrar, tampoco se puede **renombrar**. Una herramienta que escriba un temporal y lo renombre sobre el archivo final fallará al sobrescribir. robocopy y la copia del Explorador sí sirven. Hay un solo usuario de red (`jamshare`) para ASSETS y LAPTOP, así que técnicamente cada máquina puede escribir en la subcarpeta de la otra (pero nunca borrar). Si se quiere separar, se crea un segundo usuario.
- F1b (AssetSearch): **omitido** (se usa en la máquina de assets).

# Pre-jam work declaration

The jam rules (Official Rules 7(h)) allow preparing AI tools, agent configurations, MCP settings, prompt libraries and scripts before **Nov 12, 2026 at 00:00 ET**, but not building the game. Anything made earlier must be declared. This file declares it. The full log of the preparation, with dates and results, is in `PREJAM_PREP.md`.

**No game content was created before the jam:** no levels, no mechanics, no game assets and no gameplay code.

## Tools and scripts prepared before the jam (2026-11-09 to 2026-11-11)
| Item | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code dev log hook | Logs every Claude Code event as JSONL | `.claude/hooks/devlog-hook.ps1`, `Devlog/.jamroot` |
| `Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` | Installs the hook in the Claude Code user settings | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1` | Wrapper that logs every run of an external agent | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1` | Extracts agent actions (MCP, Assistant, Canvas) from the Editor log | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `New-DevlogDay.ps1` | Builds the redacted daily draft | `Tools/Devlog/` |
| `Start-EditorMcp.ps1`, `Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, `Test-UnrealMcp.ps1` | Open, close and test the UE 5.9 Editor with MCP | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `Package-Jam.ps1` | Win64 packaging and submission zip (tested recipe) | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `Backup-Content.ps1` | Daily mirror copy of the game project without build folders (the `Content/` has no git history) | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `Setup-IncomingShare.ps1` | Sets up the LAN folder where the other machines drop assets (write allowed, delete denied) | `Tools/Jam/` |
| `AssetSearch` | Local semantic search over 37,668 licensed assets (public index `codepawl/asset-index`, EmbeddingGemma 2 embeddings). Contains no assets, only metadata | `Tools/AssetSearch/` |
| Dev log templates | `README.md`, `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, this file, `PREJAM_PREP.md` | `Devlog/` |
| Project `CLAUDE.md` | Working rules for the agents | root |

## Technical tests before the jam (no game content)
- 2026-11-09: the UE 5.9 Editor MCP server answered (handshake, toolset list and a real call) in an empty project.
- 2026-11-09: built an empty C++ module (only `IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE`) to validate the toolchain. The project was deleted.
- 2026-11-09: test packaging of Epic's ThirdPersonBP template (386 MB zip, boots correctly). The test project was deleted.
- 2026-11-10: MetaHuman Animator body capture from a single phone video, driven entirely over MCP, exported to the UE5 mannequin. The test video is a raw recording of a team member swinging a stick; it is not game content and will not be used in the game. Test project: `MHProbe59` (tooling probe only).
- 2026-11-11: central machine (CENTRAL) setup, details in `SETUP_REPORT.md`: 9 PASS, 0 FAIL, 1 NEEDS-HUMAN (the cross-machine share test). Editor MCP 5/5, C++ build with MSVC 14.50.35737, test packaging of Epic's ThirdPersonBP template (385.8 MB zip, boots) and of an empty C++ module (311.5 MB), dev log hooks and wrapper verified. All test projects were deleted.

## Prompts, prompt templates or assets prepared before the jam
- (none so far; anything prepared will be listed here with its date)

## AI tools we plan to use
- Claude Code (Anthropic): main agent for code and for the Editor through MCP.
- MetaHuman Animator (UE 5.9) + the Fab plugin "MetaHuman Animator Markerless Motion Capture" (Epic, free): body animation from single-camera video, tested on 2026-11-10 with a test take that is not game content.

The Epic AI MegaJam team are people working together in the same house on a home LAN. The user asked not to be "tan quisquilloso con la seguridad": no repeated recommendations to rotate LAN passwords, harden shares, etc.

**Why:** the user found repeated security caveats (e.g. changing the 4-digit `jamshare` password) excessive for a trusted home network.

**How to apply:** mention a security point at most once, briefly, and only when it can actually break something (e.g. publishing secrets in the public dev log/git). Don't add hardening items to reports or to-do lists unless asked. Hard rules still apply (I don't type passwords myself), just state them without lecturing. Related: [[jam-central-machine]]
- [Security tone on the home LAN](security-tone-home-lan.md) — team works in one house; keep security caveats minimal, say them once

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working. Claude does not tell the person that they missed it or could not see it, because Claude cannot tell what they were watching.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, Claude usually cannot tell whether the person is reading this conversation in the desktop app, on the claude.ai website or on a phone, and the shortcut and the globe icon work only in the desktop app, so before those steps Claude says that if they are not in the Claude desktop app on the computer whose browser Claude is using, they need to open this conversation there first. Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, without guessing at what the person saw.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

content.content:
# Jam dev log (goal: the Glass Box prize for the best dev log)

Everything any agent or person does on the project must be recorded here. If it is not in the dev log, it did not happen as far as the judges are concerned.

**Language:** the Official Rules (7(i)) require every part of the submission in English, and that includes the published dev log. Write `days/*.md`, `media/` captions and `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` in English. Raw logs (`raw/`) and the team's prompts to agents can be in any language. When a day entry quotes a prompt written in Spanish, include the original and an English translation.

## Layout

```
Devlog/
  README.md                  this file (the rules)
  TEMPLATE_DAY.md            template for the daily entry
  PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md     what was prepared BEFORE Nov 12 (the jam requires declaring it)
  PREJAM_PREP.md             full pre-jam log: timeline, tests, tools evaluated, rules read
  raw/<MACHINE>/             raw automatic logs (NEVER published as they are)
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/claude-<session>.jsonl      every Claude Code event (hook)
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/transcripts/<session>.jsonl full transcript of each session
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents.jsonl                every run of an external agent
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents/<run>/               prompt, full output and diffstat of that run
    unreal/<log>.jsonl                       agent actions inside the Editor (MCP, Assistant, Canvas)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>_DRAFT.md                 automatic draft (already redacted)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md                       final entry for the day, written by a person (in English)
  media/<YYYY-MM-DD>/                        screenshots, gifs and clips of the day
```

## Rules for everyone (people and agents)

1. **Claude Code** is logged automatically by the **user-level** hooks that `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` installs on each machine. They log every session opened in the jam root or any subfolder (the root is the folder that contains `Devlog/.jamroot`). Do not disable them and do not delete `.jamroot`.
2. **Any other agent** (Codex, cursor-agent, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Gemini, generation scripts) is ALWAYS launched with:
   `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent <name> -Model <model> -PromptFile <prompt.md> -Purpose "<what for>" -Command '<command>'`
   - Use `-Shell cmd` if the command contains `< file`.
   - That is what records it. An agent launched by hand leaves no record.
3. **Prompts as files:** external agents get their prompt in a `.md` under `Prompts/`, never typed loose in the terminal.
4. **Web or desktop tools** (Fab, cloud Canvas, audio or image generators, Blender by hand): in the day entry, write down the tool, the prompt, the result and the final asset, and save a screenshot in `media/`.
5. **Unreal Editor:** always close it with `Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, which closes open asset editors first (an open animation editor crashes the Editor on exit) and collects the log. If it was closed some other way, or before deleting `Saved/`, run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1 -ProjectDir <folder of the .uproject>`.
6. **`JAM_MACHINE` variable:** each machine sets its own (`CENTRAL`, `ASSETS`…) so we know where each thing happened:
   `setx JAM_MACHINE CENTRAL`
7. **Small, frequent commits** with clear messages: the daily draft lists them. Commit `Devlog/raw/` too (the repo is private). Epic may ask for the version control history.
8. **End of day:** run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/New-DevlogDay.ps1 -Date <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Then a person writes `days/<date>.md` from `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, starting from the draft.
9. **Publish:** only `days/*.md`, `media/`, `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` and `PREJAM_PREP.md`. Raw logs may contain keys or emails: the draft is already redacted, but check it before publishing. The dev log link goes in the submission, **before the deadline**.
10. **Times in UTC.** The jam ends on Nov 15 at 20:59 EST, which is **01:59 UTC on Nov 16**.

```
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents/<run>/               prompt, full output and diffstat of that run
    unreal/<log>.jsonl                       agent actions inside the Editor (MCP, Assistant, Canvas)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>_DRAFT.md                 automatic draft (already redacted)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md                       final entry for the day, written by a person (in English)
  media/<YYYY-MM-DD>/                        screenshots, gifs and clips of the day
```

## Rules for everyone (people and agents)

1. **Claude Code** is logged automatically by the **user-level** hooks that `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` installs on each machine. They log every session opened in the jam root or any subfolder (the root is the folder that contains `Devlog/.jamroot`). Do not disable them and do not delete `.jamroot`.
2. **Any other agent** (Codex, cursor-agent, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Gemini, generation scripts) is ALWAYS launched with:
   `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent <name> -Model <model> -PromptFile <prompt.md> -Purpose "<what for>" -Command '<command>'`
   - Use `-Shell cmd` if the command contains `< file`.
   - That is what records it. An agent launched by hand leaves no record.
3. **Prompts as files:** external agents get their prompt in a `.md` under `Prompts/`, never typed loose in the terminal.
4. **Web or desktop tools** (Fab, cloud Canvas, audio or image generators, Blender by hand): in the day entry, write down the tool, the prompt, the result and the final asset, and save a screenshot in `media/`.
5. **Unreal Editor:** always close it with `Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, which closes open asset editors first (an open animation editor crashes the Editor on exit) and collects the log. If it was closed some other way, or before deleting `Saved/`, run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1 -ProjectDir <folder of the .uproject>`.
6. **`JAM_MACHINE` variable:** each machine sets its own (`CENTRAL`, `ASSETS`…) so we know where each thing happened:
   `setx JAM_MACHINE CENTRAL`
7. **Small, frequent commits** with clear messages: the daily draft lists them. Commit `Devlog/raw/` too (the repo is private). Epic may ask for the version control history.
8. **End of day:** run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/New-DevlogDay.ps1 -Date <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Then a person writes `days/<date>.md` from `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, starting from the draft.
9. **Publish:** only `days/*.md`, `media/`, `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` and `PREJAM_PREP.md`. Raw logs may contain keys or emails: the draft is already redacted, but check it before publishing. The dev log link goes in the submission, **before the deadline**.
10. **Times in UTC.** The jam ends on Nov 15 at 20:59 EST, which is **01:59 UTC on Nov 16**.

La comparación está bien hecha. Solo cambian 3 archivos y las 3 diferencias vienen de la CENTRAL. Pásale esto al agente para aplicarlo sin riesgo.

En vez del `git checkout -b main --track origin/main` del plan, que se negaría por los archivos sin seguimiento que coinciden, usa `reset` mixto: apunta la rama al remoto **sin tocar el árbol de trabajo**, y después se restauran solo los archivos necesarios.

````markdown
Plan aprobado. Aplícalo así (sustituye al checkout del paso 5):

1. Copia de seguridad: copia `.gitignore`, `Devlog/PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` y `Tools/Jam/Package-Jam.ps1` a `D:\MegaJam\_backup_presync\` con la misma ruta relativa.
2. `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main`, después `git reset origin/main` (mixto, SIN --hard: el índice pasa a origin/main y los archivos de disco no se tocan) y `git branch -u origin/main`.
3. `git status --short`: deben salir como modificados (M) los 3 archivos DISTINTO y como borrados (D) los 3 SOLO EN REMOTO (`SETUP_REPORT.md`, `Tools/Jam/Backup-Content.ps1`, `Tools/Jam/Setup-IncomingShare.ps1`). Si sale algo más, para y enséñamelo.
4. Autorizo restaurar esos 6 desde el remoto: `git checkout -- .gitignore Devlog/PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md Tools/Jam/Package-Jam.ps1 SETUP_REPORT.md Tools/Jam/Backup-Content.ps1 Tools/Jam/Setup-IncomingShare.ps1`.
5. Declaración: `git diff --no-index _backup_presync/Devlog/PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md Devlog/PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md`. Si la copia local tenía líneas que el remoto NO tiene, añádelas al archivo actual y enséñame el resultado. Si no tenía nada propio, no hagas nada.
6. Identidad solo para este repo: `git config --local user.name "Romelt766358"`. Como `user.email`, usa el correo verificado de esa cuenta de GitHub, o el noreply que da `gh api user` (`<id>+Romelt766358@users.noreply.github.com`).
7. Los 15 archivos solo locales se quedan como están, sin seguimiento. NO hagas `git add` de ellos.
8. NO hagas commit ni push. Entrega: `git status -sb`, `git log --oneline -1` y el resultado del punto 5.
````

Para que los archivos locales grandes de ASSETS (100 MB de datos de AssetSearch, un vídeo de 15 MB) no acaben en el repo por un `git add -A` despistado durante la jam, propongo añadirlos al `.gitignore` desde aquí:

- La jam empieza el 12 nov a las 00:00 ET. Antes de esa hora no se crea contenido del juego.

content.text:
Sí, quedan algunos, y conviene hacerlos antes de la 01:00. Los ordeno por lo que puede romper la jam si no se hace:

**Te tocan a ti (rápidos):**
1. **Que Unreal no se actualice solo.** Una de las lecciones del proyecto anterior fue que el motor pasó solo de 5.8.3 a 5.8.4 de un día para otro. En el Epic Launcher → Biblioteca → la flecha de 5.9 → desactiva la actualización automática. Hazlo **en las dos PCs**.
2. **Pausar Windows Update** una semana en las dos PCs (Configuración → Windows Update → Pausar). Un reinicio forzado en plena compilación o grabación es lo último que queréis.
3. **itch.io:** la cuenta unida a la jam y `butler login` en esta PC.
4. **Nombre del equipo y miembros**, cada uno con el correo de su cuenta de Epic. Lo pide la entrega y sigue abierto en `PREJAM_PREP.md`.
5. **Revisar la página de la jam:** iban a anunciar los "AI tool credits" antes del inicio, y el tema salía hoy a las 14:00 ET.
6. **Sesión de Claude Code en ASSETS:** caducaba entre el 15 y el 18 de noviembre, en plena jam. Vuelve a iniciar sesión hoy (`claude auth login`).
7. **La laptop** todavía no está preparada: `JAM_MACHINE=LAPTOP`, clonar el repo, instalar los hooks y guardar la credencial de `Incoming`. Si la vais a usar desde el primer día, conviene hacerlo hoy.

**Puedo hacerlos yo ahora (son herramientas, se pueden preparar antes):**
- **A. Script para crear el proyecto a la 01:00.** Le das el nombre y crea el proyecto C++ vacío con MCP y AllToolsets, `bUseZenStore=False`, `bEnableUncontrolledChangelists=False`, un mapa de arranque casi vacío y el primer commit. Así no perdemos tiempo a esa hora. No es contenido del juego, pero lo añadiría a la declaración.
- **B. Arreglar el borrador diario** para que no cuente las notificaciones internas como prompts del equipo. Si no, el borrador público de cada día sale lleno de ruido.
- **C. Configurar OBS** con un perfil de grabación a 1920×1080, porque el vídeo de entrega lo exige. Primero compruebo la resolución de esta pantalla.
- **D. Limpiar `Devlog\raw` de la CENTRAL** justo antes de la 01:00, para que la bitácora de la jam empiece limpia y sin los registros de este setup.

Recomiendo hacer **A, B y D**. C es útil, pero también puede hacerse el último día.

# CLAUDE.md (proyecto de la Epic AI MegaJam 2026)

Juego para la Epic AI MegaJam 2026, en **Unreal Engine 5.9.0** (CL 60351404). La jam va del 12 nov 00:00 EST al **15 nov 20:59 EST**; pasada esa hora no se aceptan entregas. El tema se anuncia el 11 nov.

## Reglas duras
- **La bitácora lo es todo** (objetivo: el premio Glass Box). Lee `Devlog/README.md` antes de trabajar.
  - Claude Code queda registrado solo por los hooks de usuario (`Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1`). No los desactives y no borres `Devlog/.jamroot`.
  - Cualquier otro agente o CLI se lanza SOLO con `Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1` (con `-Shell cmd` si el comando usa `<`).
  - El Editor se cierra SOLO con `Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, que además recoge su log.
  - Al cerrar el día: `Tools/Devlog/New-DevlogDay.ps1`.
- **Nada de código ni assets de proyectos anteriores** (en particular, nada de Panthelia). Todo se crea durante la jam o está declarado en `Devlog/PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md`.
- **Assets de terceros:** solo con licencia válida, y cada uno anotado en la entrada del día (nombre, fuente, licencia).
- **Gameplay:** tiene que ir más allá de las plantillas de Epic, y no puede ser una extensión de un tutorial oficial de Epic. Tiene que mostrar el tema de la jam.
- **Todo el contenido del juego va en INGLÉS** (regla 7(i) de las Official Rules): textos en pantalla, audio y voces, el video y los datos de la entrega. La bitácora (Glass Box) se escribe **en inglés desde el inicio** (decisión del dueño, 2026-11-10): entradas `Devlog/days/*.md`, pies de `media/`, `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md`, `PREJAM_PREP.md`, y también los **mensajes de commit**, porque el borrador diario los lista. Los registros crudos (`Devlog/raw`) y los prompts del equipo pueden estar en español; si se citan en una entrada, se añade la traducción.
- **Contenido apto para Teen (13+).** Sin marcas ni logos ajenos; el único permitido es el logo de Unreal Engine, según sus guías de marca.
- **Historial de git limpio y completo:** Epic puede pedir el historial de control de versiones y los materiales preparados antes de la jam para verificar.
- **No debe requerir software adicional para jugarse** (por ejemplo, nada de un servidor local de LLM).
- **Respuestas** al equipo en español.

## Flujo
- Prioridad: un juego jugable y empaquetado cada día, no funcionalidades a medias.
- **Empaquetar:** `Tools/Jam/Package-Jam.ps1 -Project <uproject> -ZipName <Equipo>_<Juego>`. Hazlo al final de CADA día, no solo el último.
- **Editor con MCP:**
  - abrir con `Tools/Jam/Start-EditorMcp.ps1 -Project <uproject> -Port 8059`;
  - probar con `Tools/Jam/Test-UnrealMcp.ps1`;
  - cerrar con `Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1` (nunca matar el proceso).
  - Recién abierto, el Editor responde "slow task" durante un rato: espera y reintenta.
- **MCP de Unreal:** descubrimiento progresivo (`list_toolsets` → `describe_toolsets` → `call_tool`). No inventes nombres de tools.
- **Commits** pequeños y frecuentes, con mensajes claros: el borrador del día los lista.

## Tests y verificación
Reglas que salen de lo que nos costó horas en el proyecto anterior. El porqué y las cifras están en `Devlog/PREJAM_PREP.md`, sección "Lessons from our previous project: tests and verification time"; léela antes de escribir un test o una herramienta de Editor.
1. **Pocos tests, y solo de lógica pura** que sea fácil de romper y difícil de ver jugando (puntuación, guardado, máquinas de estado, generadores, matemáticas). Toda la suite por debajo de 30 s. Lo demás se verifica jugando el juego empaquetado.
2. **Verde o rojo.** Nada de listas de "fallos conocidos", tests excluidos ni catálogos. Un test en rojo se arregla o se borra el mismo día.
3. **Cada test tiene que poder fallar:** antes de darlo por bueno, pregúntate qué implementación incorrecta lo pasaría igual. No escribas tests que copian constantes, miran el texto del código o comprueban que un campo existe.
4. **Corridas baratas:** filtros anclados (`^Game.Save.`, con `^` y punto final), varios filtros unidos con `+` en una sola corrida, y un mapa inicial del Editor casi vacío (no el nivel de juego). El nombre de un test nunca puede ser también la carpeta de otro (`A.B` junto a `A.B.C`): Unreal deja de correr `A.B` sin avisar.
5. **Mide antes de optimizar:** arranque del Editor, suma de duraciones de los tests y tiempo total. Mide el conjunto, no una parte, y compara sobre el mismo código.
6. **Nada puede costar en proporción a todo lo cargado:** ni una llamada de herramienta ni un test. No uses `CollectGarbage(RF_NoFlags)` en un test (descarga los assets; usa `GARBAGE_COLLECTION_KEEPFLAGS`), no guardes una caché por tamaño y fecha de archivo (Unreal da la fecha con precisión de un segundo), y usa referencias blandas en el Blueprint del jugador para lo que no haga falta al aparecer.
7. **UE 5.9.0 fijo hasta entregar.** Si algo falla sin que haya cambiado el código, compara primero la versión del motor en los dos logs.

Scripts de un solo uso: en un archivo, no en línea dentro de un comando; en ASCII o con BOM si son `.ps1` (PowerShell 5.1 lee como ANSI un script sin BOM); y en JavaScript, para reemplazos literales usa `split(a).join(b)`, no `replace(a, b)`.

## Entrega (checklist)
- Zip Win64 empaquetado, menor de 1 GB, llamado `<Equipo>_<Juego>.zip` y sin `.pdb`.
- Subido a itch.io y enviado a la jam antes de la hora de cierre.
- Video de gameplay de 30 a 60 s, **1920×1080 o más**, en inglés y con gameplay en los primeros 5 s.
- Link a la bitácora en inglés (Glass Box), entregado junto con el juego **antes del cierre**.
- Nombre del equipo, nombre del juego, y nombre completo y email de la cuenta de Epic de cada miembro (uno es el Team Owner).
- Assets de terceros listados y trabajo previo declarado.
- [Security tone on the home LAN](security-tone-home-lan.md) — team works in one house; keep security caveats minimal, say them once
